SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK CQL-13: CQL — Date/Time Operators Part 1. Test these items: Add (left DateTime, right Quantity), After precision of, Before precision of, Date(year, month, day), DateTime(year, month, day, ...), Component From precision, Difference in precision between, Duration in precision between. For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §8.8 Duration Between (uncertainty; official test 'years between DateTime(2005) and DateTime(2010) // Interval[4,5]')
issues.evidence: years between @1975-03 and @2020-03-01 -> 45 (crisp) on both engines; start day unknown in [01,31] so true value is Interval[44,45]. Propagates to AgeInYearsAt(@2020-03-01) with partial birthDate '1975-03' -> 45 (could be 44). Root: _duration_between_with_uncertainty sufficient-precision rule uses s_idx > unit_idx so year-duration never enters the uncertainty branch for month-precision operands, unlike month-duration which correctly requires day precision. Repro: .temp/qa/cql13_expl/probe7.py
issues.root_cause: udf/datetime.py _duration_between_with_uncertainty sufficient-precision rule treated month-precision operands as certain for year/month units (s_idx > unit_idx), unlike month-duration which correctly requires day precision; also the start-operand high boundary carried 23:59:59.999 flipping exact anniversary boundaries
issues.resolution: Certainty for year/month duration now requires day precision on both operands (interval otherwise), and date-only start high boundaries use the midnight convention; mirrored in C++ CqlDurationBetweenString; extension rebuilt+deployed (md5 57039cb04d003f65c3553d8f56fe8125)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §8.8 Duration Between; GLOBAL_RULES dual-engine lockstep
issues.evidence: years between @1975-03-31 and @2020-02-29T10:30:00-07:00: py=None, cpp='44' (cpp correct). Python path returns null when the end operand is a timezone-aware DateTime; months path unaffected (539 both). Repro: .temp/qa/cql13_expl/probe7.py
issues.root_cause: _duration_in_calendar_years/_months compared offset-naive vs offset-aware datetimes -> TypeError swallowed to null by cqlDurationBetween wrapper; C++ compares wall components
issues.resolution: _wall_clock() strips tzinfo in both calendar-duration helpers (wall-component semantics matching C++)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §8.4/§8.5 constructors: 'no component may be specified at a precision below an unspecified precision' — trailing null components are the sanctioned partial form
issues.evidence: DateTime(2024,1,1,10,30,null) -> 2024-01-01T10:30 but DateTime(2024,1,1,10,30,null,null,-7.0) -> null (should be 2024-01-01T10:30-07:00); Date(2024,null) and Date(2024,null,null) -> null though DateTime analog truncates. Both engines. Repro: .temp/qa/cql13_expl/probe5.py
issues.root_cause: translator _translate_date_constructor lacked trailing-null stripping; _translate_datetime_constructor trailing-null pop was blocked by a timezoneOffset arg at index 7
issues.resolution: Date ctor strips trailing static nulls; DateTime ctor separates timezone_arg, strips trailing nulls, treats static-null tz as unspecified, and rejects static null above a specified component (spec DateInvalid); DateTime(null) still evaluates to null
issues.verified_in: parity tests Ctor* cases + interior-null rejection test; CQL suite 1706/1706 incl. DateTimeNull fixtures
